public_rationale: The claim is that the LLM agents tested in TheAgentCompany were not close to ready for prime time. The first version of the paper, released December 18, 2024, found that the most competitive agent completed 24% of tasks autonomously (e1). It also found that more difficult long-horizon tasks were still beyond the reach of current systems (e1). This meets the contract's support condition: the best agent completed only about a quarter of the tasks, and the harder tasks were out of reach. The authors call the picture nuanced because a good portion of simpler tasks could be solved (e1). That shows some useful performance. It does not show agents completing most tasks reliably, which the contradiction condition requires.
limitations: 'Ready for prime time' has no explicit threshold and is a judgment.
The benchmark simulates a small software company. It is not a study of real workplace deployment.
The assessment covers only the systems tested in the December 2024 version of the paper.

our_interpretation: Plain reading: the LLM agents tested in TheAgentCompany, as of late 2024 to early January 2025, could complete only a small minority of realistic workplace tasks on their own. So they could not yet stand in for an employee.
The period runs from the paper's release (December 2024) to the post date.
criteria.support_condition: TheAgentCompany results at the time show the best agent completing only about a quarter of tasks, with harder tasks out of reach.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Results at the time show the tested agents completing most tasks reliably.
